transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-02
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Ng (Redwood SE), Satoshi Kim (ZenOps CTO), Priya Patel (Product), Evan Cole (Infra)

Summary:
Lena opened with quick context, Marcus took the bulk of the demo focusing on console features: per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and Optimize suggestions (batching/caching). ZenOps asked about residency, encryption, and how cost estimates map to invoices. We agreed on a pilot for three routes and to share security pack and per-route exports.

Topics Covered:
- Per-route usage analytics and how to interpret spikes
- Cost breakdown (token, model variant, cache hits)
- Routing policies and fallbacks across hosted vs dedicated
- Optimize recommendations: batching, prefix caching, quantization tradeoffs
- Security & compliance questions (KMS, audit logs, SSO)

[00:00:05] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Lena, I'm the AE on the account, and Marcus is our SE who will run the console walkthrough. Satoshi, Priya - thanks for making time.

[00:00:22] Satoshi: Yep thanks. We really want to understand cost drivers and how Redwood will help our infra team avoid surprises. We're looking at three high-traffic routes that are driving our token spend.

[00:00:40] Marcus: Great, that's exactly what the per-route dashboard is for. I'll share my screen, bear with me. (screen pauses) All right, you should now see the Console main page, the Usage tab. First panel here is aggregate tokens by day, you can slice by model and environment.

[00:01:18] Marcus: If we click into 'Routes' you'll get a list: route names, percent of total tokens, avg latency, error rate. We surface cost per route by combining model variant pricing, token counts, and any cache hit discounts.

[00:01:45] Priya: Quick thing, our route names are messy in prod - can you map human-friendly tags?

[00:01:55] Marcus: Yep. We support metadata tags and mappings so you can display friendly names in the console; it's just a label layer. We also pull service tags from your API keys if you want to enforce naming convention.

[00:02:12] Evan: How do you calculate the per-token cost when we run multi-model routing? We sometimes route to a cheaper, lower-latency model as fallback.

[00:02:22] Marcus: Good question. The console keeps per-request lineage. If a request falls back to model B, the cost attributes reflect the model actually used. For aggregated estimates we show both realized cost and conservative pro-forma cost if you had used primary model only. So you can see the delta.

[00:02:58] [00:03:05] Marcus: Here's a concrete example — this route, /compose-email, is 27% of tokens last week. We show a bar for token breakdown (prompt vs completion), model variant distribution, and a small donut for cache hit rate. That cache hit rate is applied to effective token count; we compute savings from prefix/KV cache hits and show the dollar delta.

[00:03:40] Satoshi: The cache hit number — is that automatic or do we need to enable something?

[00:03:48] Marcus: Automatic if you use our SDKs or route-level SDK config. For custom infra we expose the cache API and you can instrument KV hits. We'll show typical improvements: 20-40% token savings on conversational routes when prefix caching is enabled.

[00:04:15] [00:04:20] Priya: Can you annotate spikes and drill into individual requests? We want to understand sudden token inflation.

[00:04:29] Marcus: Yes, you can pick a spike and open the trace view. We show sample requests (anonymized) with token counts, prompt size, and eval flags. Notice the "Top Prompts" heatmap — often a bad prompt template causes a multiplier effect.

[00:04:58] Satoshi: Are the traces stored? We need retention for audits.

[00:05:06] Marcus: Audit logs are stored per your retention policy; traces can be kept for X days depending on your plan. For Private deployments you control retention duration and backing store; hosted has options up to 365 days as an add-on. We'll send the security pack with exact numbers.

[00:05:35] [00:06:00] Marcus: Now switching to Cost Breakdown — this pane shows billable tokens by route and model. We compute per-route effective price using model price * tokens minus cache savings plus additional charges (specialized kernels or dedicated capacity premiums). You can toggle to view unit cost over time and projected cost if traffic scales.

[00:06:30] Priya: Projected cost — do you do scenario modeling? Like 2x traffic but 10% better cache?

[00:06:40] Marcus: Exactly. The console has a scenario builder where you can input traffic growth, cache improvements, or quantization settings, and it recomputes monthly spend. We also recommend Optimize changes and show estimated savings with confidence bands.

[00:07:05] Satoshi: How prescriptive are Optimize suggestions? We don't want to degrade quality.

[00:07:12] Marcus: Optimize recommendations include expected latency and a quality delta estimate derived from our in-house evals on similar tasks. For conservative production workloads we recommend trying batching and prefix cache first, then quantization on replica models for background jobs.

[00:07:40] [00:08:00] Lena: Quick interjection — we've seen customers save 25-45% by combining caching and routing policies; quantization often helps more for cheaper background compute not for high-precision routes.

[00:08:15] Evan: On the dedicated vs hosted question — if we deploy dedicated pool for the heavy routes, how does the console attribute cost?

[00:08:25] Marcus: If you use Dedicated, the console will show committed capacity amortized across routes that use that pool and show per-route effective cost after amortization. There's also a view to allocate reserved pool cost by tag or route percentage.

[00:08:50] Priya: And if we have burst traffic that spills to hosted, does the console show blended cost?

[00:08:58] Marcus: Yes — blended cost is calculated: tokens served by the hosted fallback show hosted price, tokens on dedicated show amortized committed price, and the dashboard shows the blended unit cost.

[00:09:30] [00:09:45] Satoshi: Security — we need KMS integration and HSM. How far along is that?

[00:09:52] Marcus: We support customer-managed KMS keys for Private and Dedicated with envelope encryption; HSM integrations are available via enterprise package. I'll attach the architecture doc.

[00:10:10] Priya: Ok, some of this is great. For pilot scope we want three routes: external chat, internal summarization, and content-moderation background jobs. We care about latency SLOs for chat and cost for batch jobs.

[00:10:30] Lena: Perfect. For the pilot we'll set up route-specific dashboards, enable caching on chat route, and run a baseline benchmark to get reference unit economics. We'll also show how rollouts and fallbacks work in canary.

[00:11:02] [00:11:20] Marcus: Walkthrough: here's the route details page. You can set SLOs, target p95 latency, and set routing policy (latency-first, cost-first, region-first). When you set a policy, the console simulates likely model assignments and shows expected latency/cost tradeoffs.

[00:11:55] Evan: Does that simulation account for KV cache hit distributions?

[00:12:03] Marcus: Yes, you can input observed cache hit rate and the simulator will apply that to projected token counts. If you don't have data, we provide default distributions based on route type.

[00:12:30] [00:12:45] Priya: How do we get the per-route CSV you mentioned? We want to plug it into our internal cost model.

[00:12:52] Lena: We can export CSV from the Routes page. It includes timestamps, token counts, model used, cache hits, and per-request tags. I'll attach the export to the CRM and email it to the group after this call.

[00:13:10] Marcus: Also note the API has a /billing/exports endpoint for programmatic access.

[00:13:25] [00:13:40] Satoshi: A few quick risk questions: compliance for EU data residency, SSO, and audit trail integrity.

[00:13:50] Marcus: For EU residency we have hosted regions in eu-west and you can pin data region per project. SSO via SAML/SCIM is supported and we surface immutable audit logs. For additional attestations we'll share SOC2 and ISO docs.

[00:14:18] Priya: Pricing ask — can you provide an example invoice mapping from console to invoice line items?

[00:14:26] Lena: We'll include a sample invoice mapping in the follow-up packet. It shows token line items, committed capacity amortization, and any addons like extended retention.

[00:14:46] [00:15:00] Marcus: Coming back to Optimize, here's the suggestions panel. For the /summarize route it recommends batch size 8, prefix cache enabled, and switching to a 4-bit quantized replica for background jobs. It shows estimated savings: 32% monthly cost reduction with 0.5% estimated quality delta.

[00:15:30] Satoshi: That 0.5% quality delta — how do you measure it?

[00:15:36] Marcus: We run automated evals against a small set of prompts you supply and our benchmark prompts, compute n-gram overlap, semantic similarity, and human review on a sample. The number is an estimate; we recommend canary testing.

[00:15:58] [00:16:15] Priya: Can we lock models per-route? We don't want a route to suddenly switch to a cheaper variant without review.

[00:16:20] Marcus: Yes, you can pin model versions or set an approval workflow. The console supports canary rollouts where changes require approval from designated owners.

[00:16:40] Evan: For the pilot, what's the onboarding timeline? We're hoping for two weeks to baseline and two weeks to run optimizations.

[00:16:48] Lena: That timeline is realistic. Week 1 baseline, week 2 config + bench, week 3 pilot run, week 4 review and decision. We'll staff an SE-led kickoff and provide runbooks.

[00:17:10] [00:17:30] Lena: Any blockers from you folks?

[00:17:35] Satoshi: Need the security pack before execs review and need to see sample billing. Also want the per-route CSV in our format.

[00:17:44] Lena: We'll send both today/tomorrow. Marcus will include the architecture notes.

[00:18:00] [00:18:15] Marcus: Quick Q&A — Priya asked about automated alerts. The console can fire alerts on cost spike, cache drop, or SLO breach and send to PagerDuty/Slack/email.

[00:18:40] Priya: Nice. Can we add custom thresholds per route?

[00:18:45] Marcus: Absolutely. Thresholds are route-scoped.

[00:19:02] Satoshi: Any known limitations for our setup? We're hybrid cloud with private subnet for some data.

[00:19:12] Marcus: For hybrid setups we recommend Private deployment for the most sensitive traffic; hosted can still be used for public-facing routes. There are networking considerations (VPC peering, NAT), we'll include a private deployment checklist.

[00:19:40] [00:20:00] Lena: Ok let's recap next steps - we'll send the security pack, per-route export, pricing mapping, and propose pilot dates. Marcus will draft technical runbook.

[00:20:18] Satoshi: Sounds good. One last question — do you have any case studies for customers that reduced cost for high-traffic chat?

[00:20:26] Marcus: Yes, I'll link a short case study where a fintech company saved ~38% by combining caching and dedicated pools.

[00:20:45] Priya: Great, thanks everyone.

[00:20:50] Lena: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the packet and a proposed kickoff slot.

[00:21:00] (call wraps up, informal chatter for a few seconds)

Action Items Recap (from notes):
- Lena to send per-route CSV export + sample invoice mapping (due 2025-06-05)
- Marcus to attach security architecture and Optimize config examples (due 2025-06-06)
- ZenOps to confirm pilot routes and stakeholders (due 2025-06-09)

End of transcript.
